argv:
import json
from datetime import datetime

# Record the prior-art check findings
findings = {
    'date': '2026-10-18',
    'candidate': 'knitting repair planner',
    'prior_art': [
        {
            'name': 'KnittingFix',
            'type': 'commercial',
            'url': 'https://knittingfix.com',
            'description': 'AI-powered knitting diagnosis from photos/videos with human expert (Emma) escalation. Subscription $6-24/mo. Free tier: 3 AI questions/month. Paid plans marked "Coming soon".',
            'difference': 'Image-based diagnosis + human backup, not a bounded symbolic planner. Requires subscription and internet.',
            'status': 'live, commercial',
            'evidence': 'full site read'
        },
        {
            'name': 'KnitPick (UIST 2019)',
            'type': 'academic',
            'url': 'https://textiles.cs.cmu.edu/publications/2019-knitpick/',
            'description': 'Parses hand-knitting notation into graphs; transforms and combines textures; emits hand/machine instructions. Focus: designing NEW textiles, not repairing existing ones.',
            'difference': 'Design-time tool for fresh textile creation. Does not plan interventions for existing incorrect structures.',
            'status': 'academic, CMU',
            'evidence': 'indexed text, author-hosted PDF found'
        },
        {
            'name': 'knit_graph / knit-graphs (PyPI)',
            'type': 'library',
            'url': 'https://github.com/mhofmann-Khoury/knit_graph',
            'description': 'MIT-licensed loop/yarn/stitch/crossing representation and visualization. 1 star, 1 fork. Building block for machine programming and design tools.',
            'difference': 'Graph representation library only. No repair planning, no intervention sequences, no constraint validation for repairs.',
            'status': 'live, MIT licensed',
            'evidence': 'GitHub repo read, PyPI page'
        },
        {
            'name': 'Stitch Maps',
            'type': 'web tool',
            'url': 'https://stitch-maps.com',
            'description': 'Visualizes stitch connectivity without grid, shows column pathways, increases/decreases. Can knit from maps.',
            'difference': 'Visualization and charting tool. No error diagnosis, no repair planning, no intervention computation.',
            'status': 'live, commercial (affiliate program)',
            'evidence': 'full site read'
        },
        {
            'name': 'TECHknitting',
            'type': 'tutorial blog',
            'url': 'https://techknitting.blogspot.com',
            'description': 'Detailed manual repair tutorials: laddering down, cable re-knitting (structural), anchored I-cord (cosmetic). Human-authored since 2006.',
            'difference': 'Tutorials requiring knitter to understand structure. No automated planning, no verification, no adaptation to specific pattern.',
            'status': 'live, human-authored',
            'evidence': 'full articles read (cable fix, anchored I-cord)'
        },
        {
            'name': 'A Graph Model and Layout Algorithm for Knitting Patterns (2024)',
            'type': 'academic',
            'url': 'https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13800',
            'description': 'Models simple patterns as planar graphs with pre-specified edge lengths; evaluates layout algorithms against real patterns.',
            'difference': 'Pattern visualization and validation at design time. No repair, no existing structure intervention.',
            'status': 'academic (cs.HC)',
            'evidence': 'arXiv abstract read'
        },
        {
            'name': 'Laddering of a knitted fabric: topology-induced failure (2026)',
            'type': 'academic',
            'url': 'https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.20580',
            'description': 'Physics experiments + Discrete Element Rod simulations. Laddering velocity ~ bending wave speed, linear scaling with tension. Topology alone does NOT govern physical behavior (tension, friction, curvature matter).',
            'difference': 'Confirms strongest objection: topological validity ≠ physical feasibility. A symbolic planner cannot capture slack/friction/manipulation access.',
            'status': 'academic (cond-mat.soft), submitted Apr 2026',
            'evidence': 'arXiv abstract read'
        }
    ],
    'gap_analysis': {
        'what_is_missing': 'No tool takes an EXISTING hand-knit structure with a known localized error and computes a constrained, checkable intervention plan (which loops to release, in what order, with boundary/yarn-order/pull-direction validation) that preserves unaffected fabric.',
        'our_stage_a_result': 'Computational planner (A1) beats full-row rollback (A0) on 6/8 synthetic fixtures (twisted stitch, wrong crossing, yarnover, wrong type). Dropped stitches: both methods minimal (0 releases). Matches exhaustive oracle (A2) on 2/2 testable fixtures. Kill gate NOT FIRED.',
        'algorithmic_claim_status': 'Prior art (F009): minimum-cost repair planning is prior art 2007-2026. No tool found supplying intervention sequence for existing hand-knit structure.',
        'physical_validation': 'COMPLETELY UNTESTED (Stage B per Research C). Requires: 6-10 swatches, experienced knitter, measure correctness/time/distortion vs tutorial/rollback.'
    },
    'difference_one_sentence': 'A bounded, inspectable symbolic planner that computes minimal-intervention repair sequences for an existing hand-knit structure with a known error, verifying each step against topological constraints (boundary preservation, yarn order, pull-through direction), unlike image-based diagnosis (KnittingFix), design-time graph tools for new textiles (KnitPick, knit_graph), or tutorials requiring the knitter to reason about structure (TECHknitting).',
    'why_switch': 'Works offline, free, explicit checkable steps vs subscription + internet (KnittingFix); makes structure explicit vs tutorials requiring prior understanding (TECHknitting); targets existing incorrect structures vs design-time tools (KnitPick). For teachers: printable repair maps students can follow without an account.',
    'surviving_risk': 'Algorithmic advantage is prior art (F009). Physical feasibility untested (2026 physics paper shows topology alone insufficient). Input burden (user must correctly identify error location/type) unmeasured. Yarn slack/friction model missing. Stage B needs physical resources.',
    'confidence': 'source-supported (prior art), observed (Stage A result), speculative (physical feasibility, adoption)',
    'limits': 'English web search only. No patent search. No direct testing of KnittingFix AI. No access to KnitPick code. Physical validation impossible in this environment.'
}

print(json.dumps(findings, indent=2))

data.summary: Completed prior-art check on knitting repair planning tools. Found 7 relevant prior art pieces across three vocabularies: commercial (KnittingFix), academic (KnitPick, knit_graph, Stitch Maps, 2024 graph layout paper, 2026 laddering physics paper), and tutorial (TECHknitting). Key findings: (1) No existing tool computes constrained intervention plans for EXISTING hand-knit structures with known errors. (2) Stage A computational result survives (kill gate NOT FIRED: local planner beats full-row rollback on 6/8 fixtures, matches oracle on 2/2). (3) Algorithmic advantage claim is prior art (F009) - minimum-cost repair planning known 2007-2026. (4) Physical feasibility COMPLETELY UNTESTED - 2026 physics paper confirms topology alone insufficient (tension, friction, curvature matter). (5) Stage B physical validation requires 6-10 swatches, experienced knitter, physical resources not available in this environment. Decision: Knitting repair axis joins evidence base as computationally viable but physically unvalidated. Mission continues fresh exploration per STATE.md.
